Average Joes: Against real Superflex ADP, this roster's value is thinner than the names suggest. Garrett Wilson and Jayden Higgins are both modest, legitimate value at their keeper cost (2 rounds cheaper than where they'd actually go) — that's the top of the list. Drake London, currently a keeper, is basically break-even against his own ADP (2.09) at a round-one cost; he's a good player, just not a bargain. There isn't a hidden gem sitting unkept here. Given the lack of surplus, this is a team better off buying than selling — Minnesota Muskies (Jaxson Dart), Moran's Also-Rans (Michael Wilson, Colston Loveland) and The SHIELD are all sitting on real value they can only use two slots for.
Crusty Baguettes: Ladd McConkey is the one clear win here — kept at a seventh-round cost against a real ADP of 3.11, a 4-round discount. Everything else on this roster is a bigger question mark than it looks: Chuba Hubbard, currently a keeper, is actually costing 3 rounds more than his real ADP says he's worth, and Rashod Bateman and Wan'Dale Robinson are in the same boat. Worth using the keeper decision to cut bait on Hubbard rather than assuming last year's keeper is still the right one. With only one clean value play on the roster, this team should be looking to buy — The SHIELD's Tyler Warren or Moran's Also-Rans' surplus receivers are the kind of targets worth a real offer.
Draft A Better Team Tom: Rashee Rice is the headline — kept at an eleventh-round cost against a real ADP of 5.11, a 6-round discount and one of the better values in the league. The rest of the roster doesn't back him up: Courtland Sutton, also currently a keeper, is now overpriced by 5 rounds against his actual ADP, which makes him a real candidate to cut loose rather than re-keep. Combine that with the No. 1 overall pick in 2026 and this is a team that should be aggressive on the trade market rather than running it back — Minnesota Muskies' Chase Brown or Sam LaPorta, or The SHIELD's Tyler Warren, are realistic buys given the draft capital in hand.
Jack of All Trades: The cleanest keeper situation in the league. Bucky Irving and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are both legitimate 5-round discounts against their real ADP — JSN in particular, going off the board around 1.05 in a fresh Superflex draft but locked in at a sixth-round keeper cost, might be the best value in the entire league. Both are correctly already kept; there's no real decision to make there. The one flag is 2026 draft capital, with the first-rounder already moved. Given how far ahead this roster is on value, it's in position to sell rather than buy — Average Joes or and the Giant Peach, both light on top-end value, are the kind of teams that should be calling.
Middle School Mayhem: De'Von Achane and George Pickens are both outstanding, near-identical values — 5-round discounts against their real ADP, and both correctly locked in as keepers already. That's the whole story on the plus side; nothing else on the roster is close, and this team is still without a defense. Worth noting Achane's cost is already on the accelerated escalation track as a second-year keeper, so the discount will shrink before it grows. With the top two settled, the move is buying a third weapon rather than digging for a hidden value on this roster — Minnesota Muskies and The SHIELD both have proven keeper-caliber players sitting unused behind deeper rosters.
Minnesota Muskies: The most interesting keeper decision in the league is sitting right here. Jaxson Dart is unrostered as a keeper but represents an 8-round discount against his real ADP (3.02) at an eleventh-round cost — a bigger edge than either of the two players currently kept. Chase Brown and Sam LaPorta are both fine, modest values (2-round discounts each), but Dart's number says he should probably be taking one of those two slots instead. Whichever of the three doesn't make the cut is a legitimate trade chip. Draft A Better Team Tom and Crusty Baguettes, both without a real value play of their own, are the natural calls.
Moran’s Also-Rans: This roster is sitting on more real value than it's using. Michael Wilson (a 6-round discount) and Colston Loveland (5 rounds) are both completely unrostered as keepers, and Emeka Egbuka (4 rounds) is right behind them — all ahead of Jordan Love, the one player from last year's keeper trio whose number still holds up (4-round discount). Brian Thomas Jr. and Jerry Jeudy, also currently marked as kept, are actually now underwater against their real ADP. With five legitimate value plays for two slots, whoever doesn't get kept is one of the better trade chips in the league. Middle School Mayhem and Draft A Better Team Tom, both short on this kind of value, should be first in line.
My Name Is: Tucker Kraft is the anchor — an 8-round discount at a thirteenth-round cost, arguably a top-10 tight end for pocket change, and correctly already a keeper. The second slot is a real, close decision: Jake Ferguson and Quentin Johnston are both sitting unrostered with identical 3-round discounts, either a fine complement to Kraft. Notably, none of the big offensive names here (TreVeyon Henderson, Breece Hall) actually clear their own ADP — they're good players, just not keeper bargains at a round-one cost. Whichever of Ferguson or Johnston doesn't get kept is worth shopping to Tank U, Next or and the Giant Peach, both thin on this kind of value.
Seal Team Nix: Four players are currently marked as keepers here, and the real numbers say only two of them should be. Kyren Williams (6-round discount) and Baker Mayfield (2 rounds) both clear their ADP comfortably. Bo Nix is close to break-even, and DK Metcalf is the real problem — he's now costing 8 rounds more than his actual ADP says he's worth, making him the clearest cut-bait candidate on this roster. With only two keeper slots available, locking in Williams and Mayfield and letting the rest go is the correct move. Tank U, Next and Middle School Mayhem are both without a value play of their own and would be smart to ask about Mayfield if a real offer is on the table.
Surfin' Loons: Brock Bowers remains an excellent keeper — a 4-round discount at a fifth-round cost for a true top-five tight end. The surprise is that Kyle Monangai, sitting completely unrostered, actually shows a bigger discount (5 rounds) than Bowers does, even if he's a much smaller name; he's a legitimate second keeper slot to consider. Everything else, including the four-deep wide receiver room, is essentially priced at or slightly above real market value — good players, not bargains. With Bowers locked and Monangai available, this roster doesn't have much extra to sell. If a difference-maker at running back becomes available, Average Joes and Draft A Better Team Tom are both light enough on value to make a fair swap.
Tank U, Next: Drake Maye remains the headline — a 7-round discount at an eighth-round cost for a top-five dynasty quarterback, correctly locked in as a keeper. The real question is the second slot: Kyle Pitts, sitting completely unrostered, shows a 5-round discount against his real ADP, while Kyler Murray, the current second keeper, is actually running a slight overpay against his own ADP. Pitts over Murray is the better keeper call by the numbers. Running back and defense remain the weak spots on this roster regardless. My Name Is and and the Giant Peach both have spare value at those positions worth asking about, ideally using one of this team's two 2026 first-round picks to sweeten the offer.
The Flying Kites: There's real value sitting unused on this roster. Tyler Shough (7-round discount) and Quinshon Judkins (6 rounds) are both completely unrostered as keepers, ahead of Nico Collins (4 rounds), the one player currently kept. That's three legitimate value plays for two slots — an enviable problem. Whichever of Shough or Judkins doesn't make the cut is one of the more attractive trade chips in the league right now, especially given how cheap the price still is. and the Giant Peach and Crusty Baguettes, both without a real value play of their own, are the teams most likely to pay up for one of them.
The SHIELD: Puka Nacua and Amon-Ra St. Brown are, by a wide margin, the best keeper duo in the league — 10-round and 8-round discounts against their real ADP, both correctly locked in. Daniel Jones and Tyler Warren are also showing real value (3 rounds each) but sit behind a receiver room that's already spoken for at the two keeper slots. The cost: no 2026 first-round pick and no 2027 second either, both already moved. With this much value banked in two keepers, the move is patience — let Crusty Baguettes or Draft A Better Team Tom, both light on value, come calling on Tyler Warren or a spare receiver rather than initiating.
and the Giant Peach: Nothing on this roster is a true bargain, and nobody's currently marked as a keeper at all. Cam Skattebo is the best of a modest bunch (2-round discount), with Brenton Strange and Woody Marks close behind at roughly break-even. This is a roster that's going to need to build its keeper value through the draft rather than find it on the current roster. The good news is the capital to do it: a 2026 first-rounder plus two second-round picks, one via Seal Team Nix. Packaging some of that capital for a real difference-maker — The SHIELD's Tyler Warren or one of Moran's Also-Rans' spare receivers — makes more sense than keeping any of what's here.
